name: City and public spaces
purpose: the commute and travel to work, safety on foot and in public, working in public places, arriving at the office, accessibility in public, customer journeys

identity.place: The inner district of a mid-sized, temperate city along one tram line: a Victorian and Edwardian high street of three- and four-storey buildings with shops at street level and a civic library, and one block off it the converted 1920s brick textile mill that now holds offices. The tram runs along the high street on a pair of tracks set into the road. Busy but human in scale: no towers, no motorway, nothing newer than a few infill buildings of the 1990s.
architecture: the high street's buildings: red-brown brick with pale sandstone dressings (window heads and sills, string courses, a cornice), three or four storeys, timber sash windows on the upper floors, grey slate roofs with chimneys

shop fronts at street level: painted timber frames with large windows over a low panelled stallriser, a recessed door, a plain fascia board above (a slot, no words), and on some a canvas awning wound out on its arms

the old public library, set back behind a footway on the high street: pale sandstone ashlar, a plain rusticated ground floor (deep horizontal joints) to about 2.4 m, tall round-arched windows above it, a pair of timber doors up three stone steps

the mill: five storeys of red-brown brick, long regular rows of tall steel windows each of 20 small panes (5 across, 4 high) in dark green-painted bars, a deep stone plinth, a square brick chimney cut down to a stump a few metres above the roof at one corner; its office entrance is a new glazed screen set into an old cart opening under a segmental brick arch

the street itself: footways about 3 m wide of large grey concrete flags, granite kerbs about 100 mm high, the carriageway of dark asphalt with the two tram tracks set into bands of grey granite setts, overhead tram wires hung from span wires fixed to the buildings with small round rosettes; drain gullies and service covers in the flags

street fittings all painted one dark green-grey: lamp columns about 6 m tall with a slim lantern, litter bins, benches with timber slats, Sheffield cycle stands, a few bollards; signal poles in grey with a push-button box
the tram: a modern low-floor articulated tram 2.65 m wide and about 3.4 m tall, painted muted saffron yellow with a grey skirt, large windows, no logo, no fleet number, its destination display a slot
identity.materials: red-brown brick and pale sandstone, grey slate, grey concrete flags, grey granite kerbs and setts, dark asphalt, dark green-grey painted steel, clear glass, painted timber shop fronts in muted colours (oxblood, bottle green, navy, cream), canvas awnings; inside the tram pale grey panels, a charcoal speckled floor and dark blue patterned moquette; muted saffron yellow is the city's colour (the tram, the grab poles inside it, the tram stop's flag), with signal red only where it is red in life (the standing figure in a signal head)
inhabited: life on the street: an A-board outside a cafe (its face a slot), a bicycle locked to a stand, hanging baskets on a lamp column, a bin half full, leaves in the gutter
the city's systems showing: tram wires overhead, a signal push-button box, tactile paving at every crossing, drain gullies, a utility cover in the footway
slight wear: patched and cracked flags, gum marks, a scuffed shop door, a faded awning
people's traces even with nobody in the set: a coffee cup on a bench, a newspaper left on a tram seat, condensation on a cold window
scale: a person is about 1.75 m tall; a seated person's head top is about 1.3 m above the seat's floor
footways about 3 m wide; kerbs about 0.1 m high; at crossings the kerb drops flush and a strip of tactile blister paving 0.8 m deep runs across the full width of the crossing
a signal crossing is 3.2 m wide (2.4 m at least), its push button 1.0 to 1.1 m above the footway; lamp columns about 6 m tall
shop windows from about 0.5 m to 2.8 m above the footway, fascias from about 3.0 to 3.6 m; ground floors about 4 m high, upper floors about 3.2 m
the tram is 2.65 m wide outside and about 2.45 m inside, its floor about 0.35 m above the rails, its double doors 1.3 m wide, seats 0.45 m high in pairs either side of an aisle about 0.55 m wide
a mill storey is 4.2 m; its windows are 1.8 by 2.1 m; a Sheffield cycle stand is about 0.75 m high; a cafe table 0.73 m and a window bar 1.05 m high
identity.default_light: A bright autumn morning, about half past nine, with high thin cloud: soft sun low from the south-east warms the brick and the stone on the sunny side of a street, the shaded side is cool and blue-grey; long soft shadows. Street lamps are off; shop interiors glow a little warmer than the street.
identity.motifs: Use at least three of these in every scene so the sets belong to one city (each scene names the ones its camera can see): red-brown brick with pale sandstone dressings, a dark green-grey street fitting (a lamp column, a bin, a bench, a cycle stand), the muted saffron yellow of the tram, grey granite (kerbs, setts), the overhead tram wires, a painted timber shop front or a canvas awning, the mill's 20-pane steel window.
avoid: glass towers, a generic downtown or anything that looks like a famous city or a recognisable real building
real brands, shop names, readable signs, road markings with words or numbers, house numbers, flags, number plates
moving traffic or parked cars in the sets: no vehicle shows which side of the road traffic drives on (the tram tracks run both ways)
people in the sets (the cast is separate)
litter, graffiti or decay that reads as neglect; a catalogue-clean street with no sign of use
a signal pole, a lamp column, a door frame or a window edge behind a character's head
identity.outside: Beyond the streets: more brick terraces and slate roofs stepping up a gentle hill, two church spires and the mill's cut-down chimney on the skyline, low green hills at the edge under a pale sky; no landmarks.

scenes.what: the entrance of a converted 1920s brick textile mill, now an office building, seen from the footway: a glazed screen with sliding doors set into an old cart opening under a segmental brick arch, the plain brick base of the stair tower beside it with a card reader, a 20-pane steel window at the left
scenes.for: arriving at work: tailgating and access control, visitors and deliveries at the door, leaving late, the walk in from the tram

scenes.what: a long, narrow cafe in a Victorian shop unit on the high road, seen from a table near its front window: a row of small tables along an oxblood banquette on a deep bottle-green wall at the left, the counter with its coffee machine and pastry case down the right, a door to the back at the far end
scenes.for: working in public: public Wi-Fi, screens and conversations others can see and hear, leaving a laptop unattended, meeting a client away from the office
plan: Seen from above, metres: x runs across the room from the left wall (x 0) to the right wall (x 5.0); y runs from the shop front window (y 0, behind the camera) to the back wall (y 12.0); z up. The ceiling is at 3.6 m (an old shop unit), with pendant lights hanging to about 2.2 m.

Left wall (x 0): painted deep bottle green. A fixed banquette along it from y 3.0 to 9.0: seat 0.45 m, padded back to 0.95 m, upholstered in oxblood. Four small round-cornered square tables 0.6 by 0.6 m at 0.73 m in front of it, centred x 0.85 at y 3.6, 5.0, 6.4 and 7.8, each with a bentwood chair opposite at x 1.5. Three small framed prints (empty slots) hung high, 1.9 to 2.4 m, at y 4.1 to 4.5, 5.95 to 6.35 and 7.8 to 8.2. A pendant over each table.

Right side: the counter, its front at x 3.9 from y 4.0 to 9.0, 1.0 m high, a painted cream timber front with a zinc top: a glass pastry case at its near end (y 4.3 to 5.0), the espresso machine behind the counter at x 4.3, y 5.6 to 6.2 (top 1.55 m), a grinder and a stack of cups; on the right wall behind, open shelves of cups and jars and a blackboard menu (a slot) from y 6.5 to 8.5, 1.8 to 2.5 m.
Back wall (y 12.0): painted cream, a door to the back from x 3.8 to 4.7 (2.1 m), a coat rack and a tall plant left of it.

Cast spots: someone working on a laptop on the banquette at the second table (seated at x 0.3, y 5.0, head top 1.3 m), facing into the room; a second customer on the banquette at the next table along (x 0.3, y 6.4). The chair opposite the first sitter is empty with a coat over it.

Camera: x 3.0, y 0.6 (at a table just inside the front window), seated eye height 1.2 m, turned 12 degrees left of the y axis (toward the banquette); lens like 35 mm (55 degrees across); no tilt; the horizon at 46 percent of the frame height.
scenes.camera: Seated eye height 1.2 m at a table near the front window, looking down the long room and turned 12 degrees toward the banquette; 35 mm lens, about 55 degrees across; no tilt, verticals stay vertical. One strong vanishing point: horizon at y 497 (46 percent); everything running down the room (the banquette, the counter's front, the floorboards, the line of pendants) meets at x about 1352 on the horizon; lines across the room are nearly level (their vanishing point far off the left edge, x about -7716).
scenes.composition: The room recedes from the bottom corners toward the back wall, a calm cream rectangle between x 872 (its left corner, from the floor at y 685 to the ceiling at y 121) and x 1703 (its right corner, floor y 703), with the door to the back in it (x 1489 to 1649, top y 343). Left half: the bottle-green wall with the oxblood banquette running away along it (its back top falling from the left edge to x 712, y 549 at its far end), the tables in a row (table tops at x 153, y 753; x 499, y 679; x 690, y 638; x 811, y 613), the bentwood chairs opposite them (the second table's chair back about x 739, y 637 with the coat over it), the pendants above (x 499, y 109 and x 690, y 195) and the three small prints high on the wall (x -46 to 78, y up to 206; x 386 to 447, y 119 to 290; x 614 to 650, y 208 to 337). Right: the counter's front running away from the right edge (near top x 1893, y 614) to x 1563, y 543, the pastry case at its near end (top about x 1861, y 447) and the espresso machine behind it (x 1823 to 1882, top y 373); the menu board on the wall above the back of the counter (its lower edge near x 1868, y 345, running up out of the top). Free zones for the cast, nothing in front of head or chest: (1) the person with the laptop on the banquette at the second table, facing into the room in three-quarter (head top x 306, y 459; seat x 289, y 780; feet about x 445, y 960), their table and laptop just to their right in frame (table top x 499, y 679); (2) the customer at the next table along (head top x 536, y 467; seat x 522, y 718). Both heads are seen against the plain bottle-green wall above the banquette (behind points y 5.49 and 7.04 on the wall, 1.17 to 1.31 m high), each about 80 to 90 px clear of the nearest print, which hangs well above head height. What shows the height: the tall old shop ceiling with the pendants on long flexes, the menu board and the back wall's top edge near the top of the frame.
scenes.light: Main set: mid-morning, a bright overcast day. Soft daylight from the big shop window behind the camera lights the room from the front: the tables, the banquette and the sitters' faces evenly lit, fading a little toward the back. The pendants are on, each throwing a small warm pool on its table; the back wall and the door are lit warm and a step darker. The espresso machine's chrome and the pastry case's glass carry soft highlights. Shadows are soft and fall away from the camera: under the tables and chairs onto the floorboards. The room is about 12 m deep: haze 0.1 at most on the back wall.
scenes.far: The room's shell: the green wall with the prints, the cream back wall with its door, coat rack and plant, the ceiling and the pendants, the floorboards; the banquette (the sitters sit on it, in front of the far layer); the counter with the pastry case, the espresso machine, the back shelves and the menu board.
scenes.mid: The tables and the bentwood chairs along the banquette, with what is on the tables (the laptop and cup at the second table, cups and a newspaper at others); the coat over the second table's chair.
scenes.near: Nothing: the camera sits at a small table just inside the window, and that table is below the frame.
details: a laptop open on the second table beside a flat white in a cup and saucer
a coat over the empty bentwood chair opposite the laptop
a folded newspaper and an empty cup on the third table
a printed card on each table with a pictogram of a wireless signal (no words or codes)
a jar of cutlery and a stack of saucers on the counter
a tall plant in a pot by the back door
scenes.keep_first: If space is short, keep the laptop and cup, the coat over the chair, the wireless card and the newspaper; drop the rest of the small things before adding anything else.
scenes.motifs_here: a Victorian shop unit in the city's muted colours (oxblood, bottle green, cream), painted timber, the tall old ceiling

avoid: a branded coffee chain look: no logos, cup sleeves with words or a readable menu
a print, a pendant or a lamp directly behind a head
a mirror wall behind the banquette (it would show the camera)
a Wi-Fi password or network name written anywhere
uses: a consultant joins the cafe's free Wi-Fi to send a client file
a customer at the next table can read the laptop screen (shoulder surfing)
leaving the laptop on the table while going to the counter

a barista and a server, drawn with the same dignity as everyone else

the low-floor tram (outside view, destination slot)

objects.signal crossing: a signal-controlled crossing 3.2 m wide: the kerb dropped flush to the road across its width, tactile blister paving (rows of small flat-topped domes on square flags) 0.8 m deep across the full width at each end, two broken lines of square white marks edging it across the road; a grey signal pole at one side of each end with a push-button box (a slim box with a round button and a small lit panel, centre 1.0 to 1.1 m up) and a signal head on top showing a red standing figure over a green walking figure, no words
objects.tram tracks: two pairs of grooved rails, 1.435 m between the rails of a pair, set flush into bands of grey granite setts in the asphalt, the pairs about 3 m apart centre to centre; overhead, one contact wire over each track about 5.8 m up, hung from span wires that cross the street between the buildings
objects.library front: a pale sandstone ashlar front: a ground floor of rusticated blocks (deep horizontal joints every 0.4 m) to 2.4 m, a moulded band, tall round-arched windows of small-paned timber sashes above, a central pair of panelled timber doors up three stone steps under a carved hood; no lettering on the frieze
objects.shop front: a Victorian shop front: two slim pilasters with console brackets carrying a fascia board (a slot, no words) and a cornice, a large display window divided by one or two slim mullions over a panelled stallriser about 0.5 m high, a recessed glazed door with a fanlight; painted in one muted colour; some with a canvas awning on folding arms
objects.lamp column: a street lamp column about 6 m tall, dark green-grey, a slim tapered round shaft on a plain base with a door panel, a short bracket arm and a slim lantern; a hanging basket of trailing plants on a side bracket on some
objects.bench: a street bench about 1.8 m long: dark green-grey cast or steel end frames with armrests, four or five timber slats for the seat and three for the back
objects.litter bin: a round litter bin about 1 m tall, dark green-grey, a domed hood with a front opening, a door with a lock on one side
objects.street tree: a young plane tree or lime in the footway: a straight trunk about 0.2 m thick, a crown starting about 2.6 m up, in a square tree pit with a cast-iron grille
objects.low-floor tram interior: the inside of a low-floor articulated tram: pale grey wall panels, large windows from about 0.85 m to 2.0 m above the floor between solid pillars, a curved pale ceiling at about 2.25 m with a strip light along each side, yellow grab rails along the ceiling over the seats and yellow vertical poles in the door areas, a charcoal floor with a light speckle, double plug doors 1.3 m wide with yellow edges and a push button; seats in pairs either side of an aisle
objects.tram seat: a tram seat pair about 0.9 m wide: two moulded seat shells on a plinth from the floor, seats 0.45 m high covered in dark blue moquette with a small pattern of lighter flecks, high backs rising to about 1.35 m with a padded head roll, a yellow grab handle on the aisle-side corner of the back
objects.route map strip: a long thin panel above the windows showing the line as a simple stripe with round stop marks; the names are a slot, no words
objects.bicycle and cycle stand: a Sheffield cycle stand (an upside-down U of dark green-grey steel tube about 0.75 m high and 0.75 m long, set in the footway) with an ordinary bicycle locked to it by its frame: two wheels with spokes, a diamond frame, saddle, handlebars, chain and pedals, a D-lock
objects.mill front: the converted 1920s textile mill's street front: red-brown brick in English bond (rows of long sides alternating with rows of ends) on a 0.6 m sandstone plinth band; tall steel windows 1.8 by 2.1 m of 20 small panes (5 across, 4 high) in thin dark green-painted bars with a stone sill; an old cart opening 3.0 m wide under a segmental arch of brick voussoirs; a square stair tower with small high windows
objects.glazed entrance screen: a modern glazed screen fitted inside the old opening: slim dark bronze aluminium frames, fixed side panes, a pair of glass sliding doors about 2.4 m high with slim vertical pull rails, a transom at 2.4 m and fixed glass above it following the arch; a flush level threshold and a doormat inside
objects.card reader: an access card reader: a small dark rectangular reader about 85 by 120 mm with a card symbol and a tiny status light, above a round intercom button and a speaker grille, in a brushed stainless steel surround plate fixed to the wall with its centre about 1.05 m up; no logo
objects.planter: a low rectangular planter of weathered steel about 1.3 by 0.6 m and 0.6 m high, filled with ornamental grasses and a few low evergreen shrubs
objects.wall lantern: a simple black metal wall lantern: a square glazed box about 0.25 m wide on a short bracket, a small cap on top
objects.cafe table and bentwood chair: a small cafe table: a 0.6 by 0.6 m top with rounded corners at 0.73 m on a single cast-iron column and a four-footed base; a bentwood chair: a round seat about 0.46 m high, a back of steam-bent wood in one loop with a smaller inner loop, four legs joined by a bent ring
objects.banquette: a fixed bench along a wall: a timber plinth, a seat cushion 0.45 m high, an upholstered back to about 0.95 m with vertical channel stitching, in oxblood faux leather with slightly worn edges
objects.espresso machine: a commercial espresso machine about 0.8 m wide and 0.5 m tall on the back counter: a polished steel body, two group heads with portafilter handles, a steam wand and a hot-water spout either side, a cup-warming tray on top with cups on it, a drip tray; a grinder with a clear bean hopper beside it; no brand
objects.pastry case: a glass display case on the counter about 0.9 m wide and 0.45 m tall: curved front glass, two glass shelves with plates of pastries and cakes, a steel base
objects.pendant light: a pendant: a ceiling rose, a long fabric-covered flex and an enamelled metal shade about 0.3 m across, hanging to about 2.2 m
objects.framed print: a small framed print about 0.4 by 0.5 m: a thin dark frame with a pale mount, the picture an empty slot
objects.laptop: a laptop about 0.32 by 0.22 m open on a table, the screen tilted back, the back of the lid plain with no logo; the screen facing its user is a slot when it shows
objects.cup and saucer: a white ceramic cup about 75 mm tall with a handle, on a saucer, a teaspoon on the saucer; coffee with a pale pattern of milk on top
objects.coat over a chair: a wool coat thrown over a chair back, its shoulders hanging over the top rail, one sleeve hanging lower, soft folds
objects.plants: real plants drawn as their species: a tall fiddle-leaf fig or kentia palm in a pot, trailing plants in hanging baskets; leaves of their true shapes

research: Real-space facts checked on 2026-10-15 (low-floor tram widths, floor heights, door widths and seating: maker datasheets and the HCP Puma record; tram stop platforms: Croydon Tramlink stops and a Hampshire light rail report; crossings, dropped kerbs, tactile blister paving and push-button heights: UK and Irish council design standards; footway widths and kerb heights: Inclusive Mobility as cited by councils; cycle stands: York and Bracknell Forest standards; bar and cafe heights: furniture suppliers; card reader heights: access-control guidance). Sources and what was not verified: docs/research/2026-10-13-sets-city.md.
